notes: Scope judged as declared: five GitHub partitions + basic Feishu text messages as a private local read-only draft; docs correctly refuse M02/M03/M05/D07/MC24 completion claims and mark live provider behavior and independent review as pending. No fake grant, namespace, settings load, DB, model call, write or new dependency is introduced.

Static review only: I did not run tests or recompute the candidate hash. The supplied fixed evidence (254 targeted, 3508 full, Ruff clean, parent CLI probe) is consistent with the code I traced but was not treated as proof of approval.

Live-only uncertainties (not blockers; parent GH smoke should surface them as visible gaps, never as silent success): (a) `repos/{repo}/commits/{quote(default_branch, safe='')}` percent-encodes '/' as %2F for slash-containing default branches; if GitHub rejects the encoded ref the commits partition gets a `provider_failed` gap. (b) A fractional user-supplied `--end` is passed verbatim as commits `until`; GitHub documents whole-second ISO 8601, so a 422 would appear as a commits gap. (c) Feishu message list responses that omit `items` on an empty page (rather than `items: []`) would be reported as `invalid_schema` instead of an exhausted empty chat. (d) If Feishu `update_time` differs from `create_time` for unedited messages, every message would carry the edited caveat/gap and `draft_ready` would be unreachable with chat scope. (e) `--params` carries `page_size` as a JSON integer; accepted by the fake, unverified against lark-cli 1.0.56.

Repository full_name comparison is exact (case-sensitive); an operator passing a differently-cased `--repo` than GitHub's canonical name gets `repo_access_mismatch` and GitHub content withheld. This matches the spec's 'exact stable repo ID/name' but may deserve a doc line for the parent's live run.

The pulls partition has no `since` filter and enumerates until a short page or 4 pages; repositories with >200 PRs will always report `page_limit` and exit 3 even when all in-window PRs sit on page 1 (sorted updated desc). This is honest per the spec's exhaustion definition, but an optional early stop when an entire page's `updated_at` precedes window start would raise usefulness without weakening bounds.

Minor labeling: draft/unpublished releases are excluded under the `outside_window` reason (no event), which is slightly misleading; a dedicated reason would be clearer. Similarly, after `fact_limit` the collector keeps fetching further pages whose records are all rejected (bounded, visible, but wasteful).

Process cleanup: in the success path the leader is reaped by `proc.wait()` before `killpg(proc.pid)` in `finally`; the killpg still reaches surviving descendants sharing the pgid, but there is a theoretical PID-reuse race if the reaped pid is immediately reissued to a new session leader. Practically negligible for this local operator tool; noted for completeness.

Markdown projection: tabs and other Cc characters render as `	` etc., and literal `\uXXXX` text in inputs is indistinguishable from projections; hashes cover the original so integrity is unaffected, and the docs already state the projection rule.

Test quality: fixtures exercise normal mixed Chinese/URL/version/#12 content alongside malicious input, strict-after provider filtering with fractional boundaries, identity/repo change withholding, keychain failure keeping GitHub, one-chat-failure isolation, pagination cap/repeat/duplicate drift, real subprocess timeout/overflow/descendant cleanup, and a real-process CLI run with leading globals under a sitecustomize that forbids settings/sqlite/runner/adapter paths.
